extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners in ASEAN IP Offices; patent applicants, professional advisors and agents filing in ASEAN member states
extracted.subtask_description: Common guidelines that state the examination standards, formal requirements and substantive patentability criteria used across ASEAN Member States to promote convergence, work-sharing (ASPEC) and consistent high-quality patent search & examination results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language(s) in which the patent application must be filed (Question 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must file the patent application, including the specification, in the official language of the country of filing (some AMSs allow English or choice between English and local language). The language of filing is used as the language of proceedings and for amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed in a non-official language, a translation (title, abstract, claims, description and drawings) must be filed within a specified period or upon request of the patent office. Myanmar: proceedings in official language even if English selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents and information required for filing a patent application (Question 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of documents and data that must accompany a filing (e.g., specification, claims, abstract, drawings, applicant particulars, power of attorney where required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements vary by AMS; guidelines summarize common/core documents relevant to substantive examination and cross-reference national formal requirements in the Comparative Study Report (CSR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for the translation, certification, notarization or legalization of filing documents (Question 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about whether and when translations, certified copies, notarization or legalization of documents are required for filing and prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some AMSs require certified/verified translations or verification by patent agent; timing and verification procedures differ among AMSs—refer to national practice and CSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option for late filing of documents and maximum deadline (Question 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and under what conditions the office accepts late filing of documents and the maximum allowable deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National laws set different late-filing regimes; ACG-PE summarises common AMS practices relevant to substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the specification; period for submission of the translation (Question 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a translation of the specification is required and the time limit for submitting that translation to the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically required where initial filing language differs from official language; details on periods vary and are given per AMS in CSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim from multiple applications (Question 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for claiming priority from more than one prior application (multiple priority claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance aligns with Paris Convention/PCT principles; practice across AMSs summarized in CSR and ACG-PE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of filing fees per application, per claim, or per excess claims over a certain number (Question 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: How filing and claim-related fees are computed (flat fee, per claim, excess-claim surcharges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee structures differ across AMSs; ACG-PE lists common approaches that affect claim drafting strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing of applications (Question 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how patent applications and associated documents may be filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many AMSs provide e-filing; systems and acceptance of e-forms vary (some accept e-ASPEC via ASEAN IP Portal). National e-filing rules (authentication etc.) differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of a patent or utility model based on a priority document (Question 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules allowing conversion between patent and utility model/petty patent/simple patent when priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion options and timing differ by AMS; ACG-PE summarises common practices relevant to applicants seeking different protection routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period (Question 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a grace period exists for disclosures by the inventor and the scope/timing of such grace periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE refines practices where common amongst AMSs (e.g., grace period and prejudicial disclosures) and aligns with PCT/PCT GL where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required for conducting the formalities examination (Question 21 / 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data and documents the examiner needs to carry out formalities checks (completeness, filing dates, signatures, translations, fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focused on material necessary to progress to substantive examination; national formality rules vary—CSR cross-references specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejecting a patent application based on the formalities examination (Question 24 / 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal defects that may justify rejection (missing documents, incorrect signatures, non-payment of fees, non-compliant papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE lists common formality rejection grounds across AMSs and highlights remedial opportunities and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of a patent application before and during the formalities examination (Question 25 / 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how applicants may amend applications to cure formal deficiencies or adapt content during formalities checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes timing, scope, and whether amendments affect priority; practices differ across AMSs—ACG-PE summarises shared approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of a patent application after completion of the formalities examination, on grounds other than to conform with the formalities examination report (Question 26 / 2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for post-formalities amendments for reasons other than to address formalities findings (e.g., substantive amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of allowable post-formalities amendments varies; ACG-PE distinguishes pre-grant vs post-grant amendment regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic or paper-based filing of amendments (Question 27 / 2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether amendments may be submitted electronically or must be paper-based, and any formal requirements tied to the medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many AMSs accept e-amendments; national e-filing requirements and verification vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of unity of invention (Question 28 / 2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to determine whether claims relate to a single general inventive concept (unity) or require division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE defines 'unity of invention' and provides evaluation methodology, including assessment relative to prior art; aligns with international practice where common among AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications (Question 29 / 2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how divisional applications are allowed, timing, and effect on priority and prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE summarises divisional filing windows and national differences in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of obtaining a foreign filing licence before filing a foreign patent application (Question 28/2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether applicants must obtain governmental or security clearance (foreign filing licence) prior to filing abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some AMSs have foreign filing/licensing requirements; ACG-PE notes where these apply and how they affect prosecution timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordal of change of name, address etc. (Question 30 / 2.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and requirements for recording changes to applicant/owner details during prosecution or after grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes supporting documents typically required (evidence, powers), and national formalities for recordal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of a patent application before formalities examination (Question 31 / 2.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and consequences for applicant withdrawal prior to formalities examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal may be allowed at any time subject to national rules; ACG-PE summarises effects on priority and on subsequent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of rejection or abandonment of the priority application (Question 32 / 2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: How rejection/abandonment of a priority application affects later applications claiming priority from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE summarises national approaches and interplay with Paris Convention/PCT principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for appealing an objection based on formality grounds (administrative/judicial) (Question 33 / 2.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal routes (administrative and/or judicial), timelines and required submissions when contesting formality rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National appeal remedies vary; ACG-PE outlines common features and where offices provide internal reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of the application (Question 34 / 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When patent applications are published, what is published, and the legal effects of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically publication occurs 18 months from priority or earlier on request; publication content (abstract, claims, description, drawings) varies by AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of delaying or expediting the publication of a patent application (Question 35 / 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether applicants may request earlier or deferred publication, and procedures for doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE records options (e.g., early publication requests, deferral mechanisms) where available across AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information published in patent gazette/bulletin (Question 36 / 3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of information included in official patent bulletins (publication notices, bibliographic data, status updates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and format differ; ACG-PE lists common mandatory items relevant to public notice and third-party submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of claims of published patent application (Question 37 / 3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how applicants can amend claims after publication and procedural limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication amendments are allowed in many systems subject to national rules; ACG-PE summarises timing and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of granted patent specification (Question 37A / 3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how the granted patent specification is published and what it contains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes bibliographic data, claims as granted and possibly amendment statements; practice varies by AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and re-publication of granted patents in case of mistakes by the applicant/patent proprietor or the patent office (Question 38 / 3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms to correct clerical or substantive errors in granted patents and the process for re-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE distinguishes corrections versus amendments and summarises national correction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration, format, and language(s) of the publication (Question 39 / 3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of publication history, the formats used (online, paper), and languages in which publications are issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some AMSs publish primarily online; language choices follow official languages and initial filing language rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of a patent into a petty patent/utility model and vice versa before, during or after publication of the application (Question 40 / 3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and timing for converting between patent and utility/petty patent forms at different stages of prosecution/publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion options, limitations and effects on substantive examination vary; ACG-PE summarises common practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights upon publication of an application (Question 39A/3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether publication confers provisional exclusive rights or provisional protection and the scope/limitations of such rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some AMSs recognise provisional rights that may give limited remedies after grant; details are national-specific and are summarized where common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination of patent applications (Question 78 / 4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process in which the examining office assesses patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability, sufficiency, clarity, subject-matter) before granting or refusing a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All AMSs make grant subject to substantive examination; the ACG-PE covers substantive criteria in depth and aligns with PCT/EPO practices where common across AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to file a request for substantive examination (Question 79 / 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines by which applicants must request substantive examination and consequences of missing the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits differ; ACG-PE summarises typical timeframes (e.g., number of months from filing or publication) used by AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of substantive examination by the patent office of filing (Question 80 / 4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the office of filing conducts search and substantive examination itself and how the examination is performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some AMSs conduct in-house examinations; others rely on foreign offices' work products and maintain autonomy to decide grant/refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for applicants as to patent office conducting substantive examination (Question 81 / 4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant options to request examination by particular authorities or to rely on other offices' reports (e.g., ASPEC, PCT-ASPEC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains program-based options (work-sharing, PPH/ASPEC) and practical steps for applicants to request such routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of substantive examination (Question 82 / 4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and limits of the examiner's review (which patentability requirements are examined and to what depth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically includes novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability, sufficiency and clarity; ACG-PE notes variations in scope across AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for expediting substantive examination (Question 85 / 4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special procedures or requests enabling accelerated examination (e.g., PPH, ASPEC AIM, early processing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE describes ASPEC acceleration, PCT-ASPEC and national fast-track mechanisms and their documentary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of patentability of subject matter during the formalities or substantive examination (Question 86 / 4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: How patentability (subject-matter eligibility and other substantive criteria) may be assessed at formalities stage or reserved for substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some issues may be checked during formalities where relevant; ACG-PE clarifies boundaries and ties to PCT/EPO guidance where common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of substantive examination reports to third parties (Question 87 / 4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether substantive examination opinions/reports are accessible to the public or to third parties and under what conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice varies; ACG-PE notes that publication or sharing of reports (e.g., via ASPEC/WIPO CASE/Global Dossier) is a best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of the substantive examination report (Question 88 / 4.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures available to applicants to appeal an adverse substantive examination opinion or decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal routes, timelines and grounds are national; ACG-PE summarises common administrative and judicial appeal mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedure for appeal of the substantive examination report (Question 89 / 4.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific legal grounds on which appeals may be based and procedural steps for lodging and adjudicating appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural timelines, possible re-examination and whether appeals suspend prosecution; details differ by AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and information contained in the substantive examination report (Question 90 / 4.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Language(s) used in substantive examination reports and the typical content/format of those reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most AMSs issue reports in the filing language; ACG-PE describes minimum expected information (reasons, citations, objections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-grant or post-grant opposition actions (Question 41 / 4.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and procedures for opposing a patent before grant or after grant and the grounds and timing for opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE outlines existence of pre- and post-grant opposition in AMSs, typical grounds and procedural steps, and interplay with appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposition (Question 42 / 4.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated legal grounds that third parties may invoke to oppose grant (e.g., lack of novelty, lack of inventive step, lack of industrial applicability, insufficient disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed grounds vary; ACG-PE lists commonly accepted grounds across AMSs and practical evidentiary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties entitled to file an opposition action (Question 43 / 4.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may file oppositions (any third party, competitors, interested persons) and any standing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE summarises national standing rules (some permit any person, others require specific legal interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for withdrawal of an opposition (Question 45 / 4.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how an opponent may withdraw an opposition and the consequences of withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and consequences (e.g., costs, finality) vary by AMS and are described in ACG-PE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for the patent owner to respond to the opposition (Question 46 / 4.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rights of the patent proprietor to file defenses, amendments or evidence in opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE describes typical response windows and whether amendment is permitted during opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from the decision on the opposition (Question 47 / 4.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Available appeal remedies following an opposition decision and the appellate routes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines administrative and judicial appeal choices and common timelines across AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of decisions of foreign patent offices on opposition actions for the same inventions (Question 48 / 4.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how examiners/tribunals take into account foreign office decisions on corresponding applications (weight and treatment of foreign findings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE notes that offices often consider foreign decisions as persuasive but retain autonomy; guidance on how to use such decisions in ASPEC/work-sharing contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party submissions before and during substantive examination (Question 91 / 4.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and procedures allowing third parties to submit prior art or observations during examination (timing, admissibility, form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE sets out common submission windows, required documentation and whether submissions must be accompanied by translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of invention (Chapter 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: How an 'invention' is defined in legal terms for patentability assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE aligns definitions with national statutes and international standards; clarifies what constitutes an invention for eligibility assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory subject matter (Chapter 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of subject matter that may be protected by patent under national laws and common exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE lists common categories of excluded matter and cross-references national law differences; see subtopics for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods (Question 5.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of pure discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods as non‑patentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains typical exclusions and how offices determine whether a technical character is present to overcome exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schemes, rules, or methods for doing business, performing purely mental acts, or playing games (Question 5.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regarding exclusion of business methods, mental acts and game methods from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides indicators and tests to identify when such subject-matter may be excluded or, if technical contribution exists, considered patentable under some regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic creations (Question 5.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion of aesthetic creations from patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains overlap with copyright and design protection and the patentability boundary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of information (Question 5.2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether presentations of information (e.g., data structuring, formats) are patentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on technical effect tests and how presentation may be patentable if technical character is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions contrary to public order and morality, peace, security (Question 5.2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions for inventions whose exploitation would be contrary to public order or morality (ordre public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains typical scope (biological weapons, certain medical uses) and balancing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program (Question 5.2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of computer programs per se and when software-related inventions may be considered patentable (technical contribution/tests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE references PCT/EPO approaches: programs as such are excluded unless there is a technical effect beyond normal program constraints; provides practical indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for the treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy or of diagnosis (Question 5.2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion or special treatment of medical methods of treatment and diagnostic methods on human or animal bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many AMSs exclude such methods from patentability; ACG-PE summarises national nuances and exceptions (e.g., second medical use claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plants, animals and essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals (Question 5.2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on patenting plants, animals and biological processes, including exceptions for essentially biological processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE summarises national differences and interaction with plant variety protection regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmaceutical product, drug & foodstuff (Question 5.2.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific considerations for patentability of pharmaceutical products, drugs and foodstuffs (e.g., second medical use, safety exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of second medical use claims and interplay with public health considerations; national approaches summarised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'unity of invention' (Question 66 / 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal definition of unity of invention used to judge whether claims relate to a single inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE sets out the canonical definition and references tests used by AMSs and international offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of unity of the invention (Question 67 / 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical methodology to evaluate unity, including how to identify common technical features and how prior art affects unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examiner steps, consequences of lack of unity (partial search, restriction/divisional), and reference to PCT/EPO methods where shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of unity of invention with regard to prior art (Question 68 / 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: How prior art may influence determination of unity (e.g., if prior art shows only one inventive concept remains).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains interaction between novelty/inventive step findings and unity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from the final decision of the examiner on unity of invention (Question 69 / 6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for applicants to challenge examiner's final unity decision, including timelines and remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National appeal mechanisms differ; ACG-PE summarises common routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for clarity of invention (Questions 49 and 50 / 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for claims to be clear, concise and supported by the description; claims must define the matter for which protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE provides examples of clarity defects and guidance on claim drafting to meet clarity standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms not allowed in the claims and descriptions for reasons of lack of clarity (Question 51 / 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of vague, ambiguous or non-permissible terms (e.g., 'substantial', 'suitable', 'etc.') and practices to avoid imprecision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers examples and explanation why such terms are unacceptable; provides allowed alternatives and remedial amendment practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for drawings and figures in relation to the clarity requirement (Question 52 / 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for drawings/figures (legibility, reference signs, completeness) and how they support clarity of description and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how drawings should be referenced, when they must be amended to support claims and common formal defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependencies of claims (Question 53 / 7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on whether multiple dependent claims are permitted and how they should be formulated for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE summarises AMS positions on multiple dependent claims and provides drafting examples to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-part claims, two-part claims, and two-part form (Question 54 / 7.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims should be drafted in one-part form or two-part (preamble + characterising portion) and formal requirements for two-part form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE sets out tests for selecting claim format (especially for known vs novel features) and provides examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple independent claims in the same application (Question 55 / 7.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted number and treatment of multiple independent claims, and how they affect unity and fee calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains national limits, justification expectations and fee implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claims (Question 56 / 7.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for claims to the 'use' of a product or compound and the required support in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers first vs second medical use claims and drafting requirements to meet clarity and sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-process claims (Question 57 / 7.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of product-by-process claim types and when process-based limitations are acceptable as product-defining features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains examination approach: product-by-process claims may be allowable where product cannot be otherwise defined, but novelty/inventive step assessed on product per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ranges (e.g., dosage) in claims (Question 60 / 7.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: How numerical ranges should be claimed and interpreted and the requirements for support/enablement of claimed ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on endpoints, selection inventiveness, and drafting to avoid undue breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of limitations and disclaimers in claims (Question 61 / 7.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible use of disclaimers (positive/negative limitations), their admissibility and effect on clarity and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE distinguishes allowable disclaimers (e.g., to restore novelty over accidental disclosures) from impermissible ones; gives examples and form requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of imprecise terms (Question 62 / 7.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: How examiners treat imprecise/qualitative terms and when such terms render claims unclear or unsupported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests remedies: define terms in description, provide measurable parameters or examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of claims allowed (Question 64 / 7.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible claim categories (product, process, apparatus, use, etc.) and any national peculiarities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE lists common permitted claim types and notes exclusions or special formats required in some AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of amendment of a claim to also amend the description in order to meet the requirement of clarity (Question 65 / 7.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending claims requires corresponding amendments to the description/drawings to preserve clarity and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains interdependence of claims and description and how examiners handle inconsistencies arising from claim amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to substantiate the patent specification (Question 63 / Chapter 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficiency of disclosure: the requirement that the application disclose the invention sufficiently for the person skilled in the art to carry it out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE describes tests for enablement, required examples, functional disclosure, necessary experimental data, and common deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search options and databases available to applicants (Question 70 / 9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Databases and search tools that applicants and examiners can use to perform prior art searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists common patent and non‑patent literature databases and recommends best practices; notes language & IP5/WIPO resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent search for priority and non-priority-based applications (Question 71 / 9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search strategies tailored to priority-claim families versus direct national filings without priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE outlines typical search scopes for each filing route and how to identify relevant family members and prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language(s) used by the patent office in conducting searches (Question 72 / 9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Languages examiners will search and accept for search documentation and prior art submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE notes common practice (search in English and local languages where possible) and limitations affecting coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database(s) used by the patent office in conducting a patent search (Question 73 / 9.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific databases an IPO typically uses for searches (patent collections, non-patent literature sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE lists common commercial and public databases and recommends using multiple sources for completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent search parameters and coverage (Question 74 / 9.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical parameters for conducting searches (classification codes, keywords, time windows, family coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on how to choose IPC/CPC/keywords and balance recall vs precision; notes resource constraints and partial search options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the 'closest prior art' (Question 75 / 9.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for selecting the most relevant prior art document(s) against which inventive step is assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE gives indicators to identify closest prior art (same purpose/effect, similar technical features) in line with international practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the search report of the patent office (Question 76 / 9.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: What information the office's search report should contain (citations, classifications, brief commentary, relevancy codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE describes standard contents (bibliography, citations, patent family info, examiner comments) to facilitate re-use and ASPEC work-sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of a partial search and/or a 'no search' option (Question 78/9.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an office may issue a partial search or decline to search due to resource or technical constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE outlines circumstances permitting partial/no search and recommends transparent reporting of limitations in the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'novelty' (Question 10.1 / Chapter 10.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal definition of novelty and what constitutes prior art destroying novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains absolute novelty concepts and national nuances and links to date-of-assessment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining the scope of the claimed invention (Question 10.2 / Chapter 10.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for interpreting claim scope for novelty assessment (literal interpretation, equivalents, claim construction principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of claim language, dependent claims and how the description supports claim interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute novelty (Question 10.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle that any public disclosure before the relevant date can destroy novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE summarises national application of absolute novelty and exceptions such as certain grace periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters which are part of the State of the Art (Question 10.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: What types of disclosures (patent/non-patent literature, oral disclosures, public use) form part of the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on assessing whether a disclosure is enabling and thus counts as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical equivalents (Question 10.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctrine of equivalents or technical equivalents used when assessing whether prior art anticipates a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains when equivalent features may be considered to destroy novelty and relationship with inventive step assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosure or matters which do not form part of the state of the art (Question 10.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures that do not count as prior art (e.g., certain confidential disclosures, non-enabling mentions), and how to identify them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of accidental/non-enabling disclosures and statutory exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives (Question 10.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: How alternative embodiments disclosed in prior art affect novelty and claim breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE addresses combination/disclosure of multiple alternatives and their effect in anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant date to assess prior art (Question 10.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date(s) against which novelty is assessed (priority date, filing date, publication dates of prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE clarifies date hierarchies (priority vs filing) and how to treat conflicting dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person skilled in the art (Question 10.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and attributes of the notional skilled person used in novelty and inventive step assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE sets criteria (common general knowledge, normal abilities) and how to define the skilled person's knowledge base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enabling disclosure (Question 10.3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a prior art disclosure enables the skilled person to carry out the invention (impacting its value as prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE uses enabling disclosure tests to decide if a prior art citation destroys novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single and combination of prior arts to destroy the novelty of a patent (Question 10.3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether novelty can be destroyed by combining multiple prior art documents and under what circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE clarifies the distinction between novelty (typically single-document test) and inventive step (may combine documents), noting exceptional combination cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second medical use (Question 10.3.11 / Chapter 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of second medical use claims and the special novelty/inventive step treatment they receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE discusses allowable claim formats (Swiss-type, purpose-limited product claims) and national approaches to second medical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of invention (Question 11.1 / Chapter 11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundational definition used when assessing inventive step (overlaps with patentable subject matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE aligns definitions with statutory language and international guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of inventive step (Question 11.2 / Chapter 11.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal standard used to determine whether the claimed invention involves an inventive step (non-obviousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE describes standard tests (problem-solution approach, obviousness tests) as used across AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art (Question 11.2.1 / Chapter 11.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which prior art can be used in inventive step analysis and how it is formulated in the problem/solution approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consideration of common general knowledge and relevant technical teachings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for inventive step (Question 11.2.2 / Chapter 11.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and substantive tests (e.g., identify closest prior art, determine objective technical problem, assess whether skilled person would have arrived at invention) to decide inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE summarises methods used in AMSs, including PCT and EPO style problem-solution approaches and other national methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of determining inventive step (Question 11.2.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different analytical approaches (problem-solution, could-would test, hindsight avoidance) that examiners may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE compares approaches and offers practical examiner guidance to maintain consistency and avoid ex post facto reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the person skilled in the art (Question 11.3 / 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterisation of the skilled person used specifically for inventive step analysis (education, skill level, routine abilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE clarifies how to pick the skilled person's attributes in various technical fields (e.g., biotech vs software).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of knowledge of the person skilled in the art (Question 11.4 / 11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: What counts as common general knowledge for the skilled person and what literature they are assumed to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE provides indicators for distinguishing common general knowledge from specialised or obscure prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary considerations (Question 11.6 / 11.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective indicia (commercial success, long-felt need, unexpected technical effect) used as supporting evidence for inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains how secondary considerations may support or undermine inventive step findings and lists typical examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary considerations in support of the existence of an inventive step (Question 11.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive indicators (e.g., commercial success, copying, praise) that may corroborate non-obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details evidentiary standards and temporal relationships required for such considerations to be persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary considerations in support of the non-existence of an inventive step (Question 11.6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators suggesting lack of inventive step (e.g., routine optimization, industry practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE describes how such negative indicia may be weighed in the overall assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims dependency and inventive step (Question 11.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: How claim dependency affects inventive step analysis (assessment of dependent claim limitations and multiple independent claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on how to evaluate inventive step for narrower dependent claims and relationship to main claim inventive merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'industrial applicability' (Question 12.1 / Chapter 12.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement that the invention can be made or used in some kind of industry (including agriculture), and how this is tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE sets out examples and clarifies statutory tests and national variations (e.g., practical utility vs theoretical use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for appealing the rejection of a patent application based on lack of industrial applicability (Question 124 / 12.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and possible grounds for appeal when an application is rejected for failing the industrial applicability requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines common appeal steps and evidence (demonstrations, data) that can rebut lack-of-applicability findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-grant amendments (Question 126 / 13.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how applicants may amend applications before grant, scope of allowable changes and impact on priority/novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE details procedural windows, permissible content changes (no added matter), and best drafting practices to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant amendments (Question 127 / 13.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing amendments after grant (e.g., limitation, correction, reissue), and their effect on rights and third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE distinguishes amendment types, required procedures and limitations (no extension of scope), and national practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of allowable amendments (Question 127A / 13.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive limits on amendment content (no new matter, clarity/sufficiency preservation) and permitted corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to evaluate added matter and whether amendments are admissible in pre-grant vs post-grant contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments versus corrections (Question 127B / 13.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between substantive amendments and clerical corrections and the different procedures applicable to each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE explains required formalities and evidentiary standards for corrections versus amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide available work results from the priority application(s) (Question 129 / 14.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant obligations to submit work products (search & examination reports, written opinions) from the first filing office when requesting ASPEC work sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists minimum documents (written opinion/WO/ISA/IPEA/IPER, claims included) and notes English as the working language for ASPEC submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC work sharing (Question 130 / 14.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures, eligibility and documentary requirements for requesting ASEAN Patent Examination Cooperation assistance (ASPEC) and accelerated examination using another AMS's work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes ASPEC request forms, local agent requirements in some AMSs, mandatory enclosure of written opinions/search/examination reports, and how ASPEC acceleration/work-sharing commences once all requisite documents are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requests for information or documents apart from documents/information required under ASPEC (Question 131 / 14.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the second IP Office may request documents beyond ASPEC minimums and what additional verifications some AMSs may demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: verified English translations (Cambodia), proof of publication and substantive exam fee payment (Indonesia), Thai translations of reports (Thailand). ACG-PE highlights national variances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-use of search and examination results of other offices (Question 133 / 14.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible modes for re-using search & examination work products from other patent offices (modified examination, unilateral reuse, PPHs, validation), and best practices to support work-sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE encourages publication of S&E outputs (best practice) and references international systems (WIPO CASE, IP5 Global Dossier, CCD) that facilitate secure sharing and re-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC/PCT-ASPEC request procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: How to make ASPEC and PCT-ASPEC requests, what to indicate on forms (e.g., PCT-ASPEC remark), and additional communication steps (email monitoring authority/focal point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum documents include copy of ISA/IPEA report and at least one claim found allowable by first office; requests may be made up to final decision and e-ASPEC may replace separate forms where supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory requirements for filing an ASPEC application (table summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Country-by-country practical requirements for ASPEC (need for local agent, necessity to enclose written opinion, claim correspondence table, hardcopy form requirements, e-ASPEC availability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE provides a summary table per AMS showing specific local filing practices and mandatory procedural steps; applicants must consult national rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of international work-sharing tools (WIPO CASE, Global Dossier, IP5 CCD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on leveraging international repositories and tools to access and share search and examination documentation across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains 'accessing' vs 'providing' office roles in WIPO CASE, current participation levels, and how CCD consolidates citation data to aid examiners in identifying prior art and family citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and publication as best practice for work-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that patent offices publish S&E information (legal status, reports) online to facilitate examination by other offices and support work-sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: European Patent Register; ACG-PE treats such publication as best practice to improve re-use and backlog mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of ACG-PE with national law and CSR (scope & disclaimer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that ACG-PE summarises common AMS practices within CSR scope but is not a legal authority; applicants should refer to national legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACG-PE is based on CSR and PCT/EPO practices and is intended as harmonizing guidance—national differences persist and must be consulted for binding requirements.
